content.title: About
content.content: Meatless vegetable lasagna is a layered Italian dish that replaces traditional ground meat with a mix of fresh vegetables (bell pepper, zucchini, eggplant, carrot) and tomato sauce, topped with mozzarella and parmesan cheese. The dish is rich in vitamins, fiber, and plant‑based protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetarian lasagna is often enriched with soy mince or tofu to boost protein content.
Traditional Italian lasagna dates back to medieval Italy, originally made with sheets of pasta, cheese, and sauce.
Adding vegetables makes the dish lighter and reduces calories compared with meat versions.
Gluten‑free versions use rice‑ or corn‑flour sheets instead of wheat pasta.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: The vegetables provide vitamin C, vitamin A (as beta‑carotene) and folate, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Plant protein
items.content: Tofu or soy mince adds complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Absence of meat and use of low‑fat cheeses reduces saturated fat, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and red peppers contain lycopene and vitamin E, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Tofu and soy mince can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheeses and ready‑made tomato sauces are often high in salt; choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Calorie load from excess cheese
items.content: Using large amounts of mozzarella and parmesan raises calories and saturated fat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Parboil the lasagna sheets, sauté the vegetables, combine them with tomato sauce and soy mince, layer with cheese, and bake for 25‑30 minutes at 180 °C until golden. Serve hot, garnished with fresh basil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked lasagna in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, portion, seal in freezer bags and freeze up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge before reheating.
